questions.stem: Point P has coordinates $(-3,\ 2)$, and point Q has coordinates $(15,\ -8)$. Point M is the midpoint of $[\text{PQ}]$.

parts.label: b
parts.intro: Line $L$ is perpendicular to $[\text{PQ}]$ and passes through M.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence, write down the equation of $L$.

questions.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{7x + 7}{2x - 4}$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $x \neq 2$.

parts.label: b
parts.markscheme:
(i) $x = 2$ (must be an equation with $x$) ***A1***

(ii) $y = \dfrac{7}{2}$ (must be an equation with $y$) ***A1***

parts.label: c
parts.markscheme:
**EITHER**

interchanging $x$ and $y$ ***(M1)***

$2xy - 4x = 7y + 7$

correct working with $y$ terms on the same side: $2xy - 7y = 4x + 7$ ***(A1)***

**OR**

$2yx - 4y = 7x + 7$

correct working with $x$ terms on the same side: $2yx - 7x = 4y + 7$ ***(A1)***

interchanging $x$ and $y$ OR making $x$ the subject $x = \dfrac{4y + 7}{2y - 7}$ ***(M1)***

**THEN**

$f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4x + 7}{2x - 7}$ (or equivalent) $\left(x \neq \dfrac{7}{2}\right)$ ***A1***

questions.stem:
On a Monday at an amusement park, a sample of $40$ visitors was randomly selected as they were leaving the park. They were asked how many times that day they had been on a ride called *The Dragon*. This information is summarized in the following frequency table.

| **Number of times on *The Dragon*** | **Frequency** |
|:---:|:---:|
| $0$ | $6$ |
| $1$ | $16$ |
| $2$ | $13$ |
| $3$ | $2$ |
| $4$ | $3$ |

It can be assumed that this sample is representative of all visitors to the park for the following day.

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
(i) summing frequencies of riders or finding complement ***(M1)***

probability $= \dfrac{34}{40}$ ***A1***

(ii) attempt to find expected value ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{16}{40} + \left(2 \times \dfrac{13}{40}\right) + \left(3 \times \dfrac{2}{40}\right) + \left(4 \times \dfrac{3}{40}\right)$

$\dfrac{60}{40} \ (= 1.5)$ ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.intro: It is known that $1000$ visitors will attend the amusement park on Tuesday. *The Dragon* can carry a maximum of $10$ people each time it runs.
parts.text: Estimate the minimum number of times *The Dragon* must run to satisfy demand.
parts.markscheme:
evidence of **their** rides per visitor $\times 1000$ or $\div 10$ ***(M1)***

$1500$ OR $0.15$

$150$ (times) ***A1***

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the equation $\cos 2x = \sin x$ can be written in the form $2\sin^2 x + \sin x - 1 = 0$.

parts.label: b
parts.markscheme:
valid attempt to solve quadratic ***(M1)***

$(2\sin x - 1)(\sin x + 1)$ OR $\dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 4(2)(-1)}}{2(2)}$

recognition to solve for $\sin x$ ***(M1)***

$\sin x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ OR $\sin x = -1$

any correct solution from $\sin x = -1$ ***A1***

any correct solution from $\sin x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ ***A1***

> **Note:** The previous two marks may be awarded for degree or radian values, irrespective of domain.

$x = -\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ ***A1***

> **Note:** If no working shown, award no marks for a final value(s).  
> Award ***A0*** for $-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ if additional values also given.

parts.text: Find the range of possible values of $k$ such that $e^{2x} + \ln k = 3e^x$ has at least one real solution.
parts.markscheme:
recognition of quadratic in $e^x$ ***(M1)***

$\left(e^x\right)^2 - 3e^x + \ln k \ (= 0)$ OR $A^2 - 3A + \ln k \ (= 0)$

recognizing discriminant $\geq 0$ (seen anywhere) ***(M1)***

$(-3)^2 - 4(1)(\ln k)$ OR $9 - 4\ln k$ ***(A1)***

$\ln k \leq \dfrac{9}{4}$ ***(A1)***

$e^{\frac{9}{4}}$ (seen anywhere) ***A1***

$0 < k \leq e^{\frac{9}{4}}$ ***A1***

questions.stem:
The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = \sin qx$, where $q > 0$. The following diagram shows part of the graph of $f$ for $0 \leq x \leq 4m$, where $x$ is in radians. There are $x$-intercepts at $x = 0$, $2m$ and $4m$.

![Grid with x from 0 to 6m and y from −4 to 4, showing one period of f: maximum 1 at x = m, minimum −1 at x = 3m.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz1-q6.png)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find an expression for $m$ in terms of $q$.
parts.markscheme:
recognition that period is $4m$ OR substitution of a point on $f$ (except the origin) ***(M1)***

$4m = \dfrac{2\pi}{q}$ OR $1 = \sin qm$

$m = \dfrac{\pi}{2q}$ ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.intro: The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = 3\sin\dfrac{2qx}{3}$, for $0 \leq x \leq 6m$.
parts.text: On the axes above, sketch the graph of $g$.
parts.markscheme:
horizontal scale factor is $\dfrac{3}{2}$ (seen anywhere) ***(A1)***

> **Note:** This ***(A1)*** may be earned by seeing a period of $6m$, half period of $3m$ or the correct $x$-coordinate of the maximum/minimum point.

![Graph of g: amplitude 3, maximum (1.5m, 3), zero at 3m, minimum (4.5m, −3), ending at 6m, drawn with the graph of f.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p1-tz1-q6b-ms.png)

***A1A1A1***

> **Note:** Curve must be an approximate sinusoidal shape (sine or cosine). Only in this case, award the following:  
> ***A1*** for correct amplitude.  
> ***A1*** for correct domain.  
> ***A1*** for correct max and min points **and** correct $x$-intercepts.
